kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-01.title: Compute
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-01.body:
The values are $201$, $20$, $2011$, $2012$ and $\frac{1}{2011}$. The biggest is $1 + 2011 = 2012$ (multiplying by 1 does not change a number, but adding 1 does).

**Answer: (D) $1+2011$**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-02.title: Count faces
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-02.body:
A tetrahedron has 4 faces and a die (cube) has 6. Total: $3\cdot4 + 5\cdot6 = 12 + 30 = 42$.

**Answer: (A) 42**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-03.title: Count stripes
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-03.body:
Starting and ending with white, 8 white stripes have 7 black stripes between them: 15 stripes. $15 \cdot 50$ cm $= 750$ cm $= 7.5$ m.

**Answer: (B) 7.5 m**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-05.title: Next possible time
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-05.body:
Starting with 20, the remaining digits 1, 1 only give 20:11. Next hour 21: the minutes use 0 and 1, so 21:01 or 21:10. The first one is 21:01, which is 50 minutes after 20:11.

**Answer: (C) 50**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-06.title: Each square is half the next
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-06.body:
Joining the midpoints of a square's sides cuts off 4 corner triangles which together are as big as the inner square, so the inner square has half the area. Small 6, middle 12, big 24 cm².

**Answer: (A) 24 cm²**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-06.title: Fold the corners
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-06.body:
Fold the four corner triangles of the big square inwards: they exactly cover the middle square. So big $= 2\times$ middle $= 4\times$ small $= 24$ cm².

**Answer: (A) 24 cm²**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-07.title: Count each side
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-07.body:
The even side has $2, 4, \dots, 12$: 6 houses. So the odd side has $17 - 6 = 11$ houses: $1, 3, \dots$; the 11th odd number is $2\cdot11 - 1 = 21$.

**Answer: (E) 21**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-08.title: Bound the third day
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-08.body:
Let the days be $a < b < c$ with $c < a + b$ and $a+b+c = 12$. From $c < a+b = 12 - c$ we get $c < 6$. Also $c$ is the largest of three different numbers adding to 12, so $c \ge 5$ (if $c \le 4$ the total would be at most $4+3+2 = 9$). So $c = 5$ (e.g. 3, 4, 5).

**Answer: (A) 5**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-09.title: Find both
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-09.body:
Smallest: make the hundreds digit as small as possible (1), then the tens digit (0): $107$. Largest: put all 8 in the hundreds: $800$. Sum $107 + 800 = 907$.

**Answer: (B) 907**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-10.title: Try every position
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-10.body:
The new square must share a side with the L. Going through the possible places:

- to the right of the bottom-right square: a big L with equal arms, symmetric about the diagonal ✓
- to the left of the bottom-left square: a T shape ✓
- to the right of the top square: a U shape (C shape) ✓
- any other place (above, below, inside the corner, next to the middle square, under the right square): no line of symmetry.

So there are 3 ways.

**Answer: (C) 3**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-11.title: Count decimal places
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-11.body:
Write each number with 2011: numerator $2011 \cdot \frac{2011}{1000}$, denominator $\frac{2011}{10}\cdot\frac{2011}{100} = \frac{2011^2}{1000}$. Numerator and denominator are both $\frac{2011^2}{1000}$, so the value is 1.

**Answer: (C) 1**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-12.title: Pair the pearls
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-12.body:
- $17 = 8 + 9$ (the only way).
- $13 = 6 + 7$ or $4 + 9$ or $5 + 8$; 8 and 9 are used, so $6 + 7$.
- $7 = 1 + 6$ or $2 + 5$ or $3 + 4$; 6 is used.
- $5 = 1 + 4$ or $2 + 3$.

If $7 = 3 + 4$, then 5 cannot be made (needs 1+4 or 2+3). So $7 = 2 + 5$ and $5 = 1 + 4$, leaving the 3 g pearl.

**Answer: (C) 3 g**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-12.title: Use the total
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-12.body:
All pearls weigh $45$ g; the rings weigh $17+13+7+5 = 42$ g, so the unused pearl weighs $45 - 42 = 3$ g (one can check the pairing $8+9, 6+7, 2+5, 1+4$ works).

**Answer: (C) 3 g**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-13.title: Colour the seeds like a chessboard
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-13.body:
The seeds sit on a square grid (rows: 1 seed in the entrance, then 3, 5 and 7 seeds). Colour them alternately black and white like a chessboard, so that every step along the path goes from one colour to the other. The entrance seed and the exit seed (bottom right) are both black.

- The seed at the far left end of the bottom row lies in a dead end: Fridolin would have to go back through the junction next to it, so he can never collect it.
- Of the other 15 seeds, 9 are black and 6 are white. Since colours alternate and the path starts and ends on black, it visits at most $6$ white and $7$ black seeds: at most $13$.

13 is possible: enter, go left along the top row, down, left along the second row, down, right along the bottom row to the middle, up, right along the second row to its end, down and out to the exit.

**Answer: (B) 13**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-14.title: Remove two with the same average
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-14.body:
The sum is $96$ for 8 scores, so the average is $12$. Removing two scores keeps the average exactly when the two have average 12, i.e. sum 24. Only $14 + 10 = 24$.

**Answer: (E) 14 and 10**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-15.title: Work outwards
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-15.body:
- The L-shaped area around R, G and O touches all three, so it is **blue**.
- The strip below R, G, O touches G, O and the blue area, so it is **red**.
- The tall strip to the right of O touches O, blue and red, so it is **green**.
- The big outer L (top and left) touches blue, red and green, so it is **orange**.
- The bottom strip touches orange, red and green, so it is **blue**.
- X touches orange (top), blue (bottom strip) and green, so X is **red**.

**Answer: (A) red**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-16.title: Count each cut twice
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-16.body:
Let the side be $s$. The total perimeter of the pieces is the outer boundary ($4s$) plus each cut counted twice (it borders two pieces). The cuts are one vertical line of length $s$ and two horizontal cuts on each side, which together have length $2s$. So the total is $4s + 2(s + 2s) = 10s = 120$, giving $s = 12$ cm and area $144$ cm².

**Answer: (D) 144 cm²**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-17.title: Where did the goal against go?
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-17.body:
In the lost game Barcelona conceded at least one goal more than it scored, so the only goal against was in that game: it was lost 0:1. Then the draw had no goals conceded, so it was 0:0. All 3 goals were scored in the win, which was 3:0.

**Answer: (B) 3:0**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-18.title: By position of the right angle
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-18.body:
The area is $\frac12\cdot 2\cdot h = 1$, so $F$ is at distance $h = 1$ from line $DE$.

- Right angle at $D$: $F$ on the perpendicular at $D$, 1 cm away: 2 points.
- Right angle at $E$: likewise 2 points.
- Right angle at $F$: $F$ is on the circle with diameter $DE$ (radius 1), at distance 1 from $DE$: the top and bottom points of the circle, 2 points.

Total 6.

**Answer: (C) 6**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-19.title: Compare with b
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-19.body:
Multiplying $b$ by $a < 1$ makes it smaller: $ab < b$. Dividing $a$ by $b > 1$ gives $a/b < a < 1 < b$. Adding a positive $a$ makes it bigger: $a + b > b$. So $a + b$ is the biggest.

**Answer: (B) $a+b$**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-19.title: Try numbers
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-19.body:
With $a = \frac12$, $b = 2$: $ab = 1$, $a+b = 2.5$, $a\div b = 0.25$, $b = 2$. The largest is $a+b$, and the argument above shows this always happens.

**Answer: (B) $a+b$**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-20.title: Follow the line around the cube
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-20.body:
The line goes around the four side faces of the cube. On the first face it runs straight from a bottom corner to the midpoint of the opposite vertical edge, on the second from that midpoint to the top corner, on the third from that top corner down to the midpoint of the next edge, and on the fourth from there back down to the starting corner.

In the net the four side faces lie in a row, so the line must start at a bottom corner, pass the first fold exactly at its midpoint, reach the top at the second fold, pass the third fold at its midpoint and end at the bottom corner — two straight segments forming a roof shape through the midpoints. Only net A shows this (in B, C and D the line crosses the folds at the wrong heights; in E it uses the wrong faces).

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-21.title: Divisibility rules
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-21.body:
Divisible by 5: $Y = 0$ or $5$; divisible by 4: the number is even, so $Y = 0$ (and $80$ is divisible by 4 ✓). Divisible by 9: the digit sum $2+4+X+8+0 = 14 + X$ must be a multiple of 9, so $X = 4$. Then $X + Y = 4$.

**Answer: (E) 4**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-22.title: Block the middle
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-22.body:
The free cells are a $3\times3$ block in the middle (plus one cell above it), the three left cells of the fourth row and the whole bottom row.

Place counter D (the T shape) with its bar across the middle row of the free $3\times3$ block and its stem going down through the fourth and fifth rows (the middle column). The free cells that are left split into three separate pieces of only 4, 4 and 2 cells (above the bar, the $2\times2$ corner on the left, and the right end of the bottom row). Every counter has 5 cells, so none of them fits anymore.

For each of the other counters one can check that wherever it is placed, at least one of the remaining counters still fits.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-23.title: Triangle inequality
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-23.body:
Write $IM$, $IO$, $MO$ for the distances between the nests.

- If Max and Oskar both told the truth: $MO > 2\,IM$ and $MO > 2\,IO$, so $MO > IM + IO$ — impossible, because going from $M$ to $O$ via $I$ is never shorter than going directly.
- If Isaak and Max both told the truth: $IM > 2\,IO$ and $MO > 2\,IM$. But $MO \le IM + IO < IM + \frac12 IM < 2\,IM$ — impossible.

So Max cannot be truthful together with either of the others; since two tell the truth, they are Isaak and Oskar (possible: Isaak and Oskar close together, Max far away). Max is lying.

**Answer: (B) Max**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-24.title: Add and subtract the overlaps
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-24.body:
Let $P$ be the overlap of the 5-square with the 7-square, and $Q$ the overlap of the 3-square with the 5-square (which lies inside the 7-square).

- Black = the 7-square minus everything covered by the other two squares: $49 - 9 - P + Q$.
- Grey = the part of the 5-square outside the 7-square plus the overlap with the 3-square: $(25 - P) + Q$.

Difference: $(49 - 9 - P + Q) - (25 - P + Q) = 49 - 9 - 25 = 15$ cm², whatever the overlaps are.

**Answer: (D) 15 cm²**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-25.title: Find the hits
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-25.body:
Let him hit 8 and 10 each $k$ times and 5 $m$ times: $18k + 5m = 99$. Since $5m$ is a multiple of 5, $18k$ must end in 4 or 9: $k = 3$ gives $54$, so $5m = 45$, $m = 9$ ($k = 8$ would already exceed 99). Hits: $3 + 3 + 9 = 15$. These are 75% of his shots, so he shot $15 \div 0.75 = 20$ times.

**Answer: (D) 20**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-26.title: Find a circle
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-26.body:
In triangle $ABC$, $AB = AC$, so $\angle ACB = 75^\circ$ and $\angle BAC = 30^\circ$. Then $\angle CAD = 80^\circ - 30^\circ = 50^\circ$, and in triangle $ACD$: $\angle ACD = 180^\circ - 50^\circ - 65^\circ = 65^\circ = \angle ADC$, so $AD = AC$.

Thus $AB = AC = AD$: $B$, $C$, $D$ lie on a circle centred at $A$. The inscribed angle $\angle BDC$ stands on the same arc $BC$ as the central angle $\angle BAC = 30^\circ$, so $\angle BDC = 15^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) $15^\circ$**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-26.title: Isosceles triangle ABD
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-26.body:
With $AB = AD$ (shown above) triangle $ABD$ is isosceles with apex angle $80^\circ$, so $\angle ADB = 50^\circ$. Then $\angle BDC = \angle ADC - \angle ADB = 65^\circ - 50^\circ = 15^\circ$.

**Answer: (B) $15^\circ$**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-27.title: Remainders
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-27.body:
Eva: $E - 7$ is a multiple of 8, so $E + 1$ is a multiple of 8; $E + 8$ is a multiple of 7, so $E + 1$ is a multiple of 7. Hence $E + 1$ is a multiple of 56: $E = 55, 111, \dots$

Raffi: $R - 8$ is a multiple of 7 and $R + 7$ a multiple of 8, so $R - 1$ is a multiple of 7 and of 8, i.e. of 56: $R = 57, 113, \dots$ (he is at least 8).

So $R - E = 2 + 56k$ for some whole number $k$. Of the choices only “Raffi is two years older” ($R = 57$, $E = 55$) fits.

**Answer: (A) Raffi is two years older than Eva.**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-28.title: Cancel and estimate
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-28.body:
Cancel $G$ and one $A$: the value is $\dfrac{K\cdot A\cdot N\cdot R\cdot O^2}{M\cdot E}$, with eight different non-zero digits $K, A, N, G, R, O, M, E$.

**Value 1 is impossible:** the denominator is at most $9\cdot 8 = 72$. In the numerator, if $O = 1$ the other four are different digits at least 2, giving at least $2\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5 = 120$; if $O \ge 2$ it is at least $1\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot 2^2 = 240$. So the numerator is always bigger than the denominator.

**Value 2 works:** $O = 1$, $\{K, A, N, R\} = \{2, 3, 4, 6\}$, $\{M, E\} = \{8, 9\}$, $G = 5$: $\frac{2\cdot3\cdot4\cdot6}{8\cdot9} = \frac{144}{72} = 2$.

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-29.title: Follow the two moves
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-29.body:
The bottom width of the figure is $11 + 13 = 24$.

- The lower right triangle (legs 24 along the bottom and the lower part of the right side) is turned half a turn about the marked point on the right side. Its 24-long bottom edge then continues the horizontal step edge (length 13) beyond its corner, giving a horizontal line of length $13 + 24 = 37$ in the triangle.
- The left triangle (legs 11 and $x$) is turned a quarter turn about the top marked point: its leg 11 goes along the vertical edge below that point, and its leg $x$ lies exactly along that horizontal line, ending at the far corner of the big triangle.

So $x = 13 + 24 = 37$.

**Answer: (B) 37**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-30.title: 10 clicks are enough
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-30.body:
Colour the board like a chessboard. Every pair of side-neighbours contains exactly one black cell, so one blue cell is black. Click the 8 black cells in this order: first the 2 in the middle (4 neighbours each), then the 4 on the edges (3 neighbours), then the 2 corners (2 neighbours). As soon as a black cell is blue, the other blue cell is one of its white neighbours; click them one after another.

- Blue found at click 1 or 2: at most 4 more clicks.
- At click 3–6: at most 3 more, total at most 9.
- At click 7 or 8: at most 2 more, total at most 10.

(If 7 black cells are red, the 8th must be blue, but it still has to be clicked.)

**Answer: (B) 10**

kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-30.title: 9 clicks are not enough
kangaroo-at-2011-kadett-30.body:
Suppose the game always answers “red” as long as possible. Any 9 cells of the board contain at least two side-neighbour pairs (8 cells without neighbours must be one chessboard colour, and any 9th cell touches at least two of them). So after 7 red clicks, at least two possible blue pairs remain among the unclicked cells.

With two possible pairs left, 2 more clicks are never certain: if the next click is on a cell belonging to only one of the pairs, the answer can be “red” and then the other pair still needs 2 clicks; if it is on a cell shared by both pairs (blue), the next click can be “red” and then one more cell has to be clicked. So at least $7 + 3 = 10$ clicks are needed.

**Answer: (B) 10**
